1

Download the lab base and unzip it

Before Part A
Animated screens drawn for this guide; the terminal outputs are the real outputs of the scripts. Click the picture to enlarge.
  • In Léa › Documents (or the Class 3 lecture module › Tables and files), download 420-1C2-DW_Class03_Code_Schematics_Tables.zip and the Class 2 package.
  • Before you click: read the address letter by letter, scan the link with VirusTotal, check the domain with Google Safe Browsing — open only files that come from Léa or from the lecture module.
  • Right-click the ZIP › Extract All… (Windows) or double-click it (macOS). You get code/example1…4 with their inputs and expected_output/, lab1/ with the workbook and a sample folder, the drawings and the tables.
Rule: Legal Notice 14.2 and Annex C: check every link and every file before you trust it; download only from official sources; if in doubt, do not click.
Versions and look (October 2026): Screens drawn for this guide. Windows 11 (version 25H2, October 2026) shows Extract All… in the right-click menu; older Windows 10 menus show the same entry. On macOS, Finder extracts a ZIP with a double-click. Léa's page layout depends on your college's version of Omnivox.
2

Create the folder and write the README

Part A — 5 points
Animated screens drawn for this guide; the terminal outputs are the real outputs of the scripts. Click the picture to enlarge.
  • One command creates the folder and its three sub-folders. Replace Lastname_Firstname by your own names, without spaces or accents.
  • mkdir -p Lab1_Lastname_Firstname/{workbook/csv,diagrams,memo} (Git Bash, macOS, Linux) — or in PowerShell: mkdir Lab1_Lastname_Firstname\workbook\csv, Lab1_Lastname_Firstname\diagrams, Lab1_Lastname_Firstname\memo
  • Write README.txt at the top of the folder: course and lab title · Student · Student number · Date · Sources · Tools · the integrity statement, word for word: I used fictional lab data only. Then copy 420-1C2-DW_Lab1_Kalmia_Workbook.xlsx into workbook/.
Rule: Legal Notice 18.2: by submitting, you confirm that the work was produced only in an authorized lab environment and contains no real personal information — the README states it.
Versions and look (October 2026): Git for Windows 2.56.0 (October 2026) installs Git Bash; its prompt looks different from the one drawn here. Notepad, TextEdit (plain text mode) or VS Code all write the README; save it as UTF-8.
3

Run code example 1 — the business impact analysis

Part D — 20 points
Animated screens drawn for this guide; the terminal outputs are the real outputs of the scripts. Click the picture to enlarge.
  • In a terminal: cd code/example1_business_impact_analysis then python kalmia_bia.py bia_processes.csv bia_impacts.csv bia_dependencies.csv recovery_capability.csv
  • The script prints one line per step: [IMPACT] and [RTO] give the MTD (maximum tolerable downtime), the RTO (recovery time objective) and the tier of each process; [DEP] tests every dependency; [BACKUP], [SPOF] (single point of failure) and [RANK] close the run.
  • Two files appear next to the script: critical_services_register.csv → sheet Critical services; dependency_gaps.csv → sheet Dependencies. Compare with expected_output/. Rule to check: RTO < MTD for every process.
Rule: Legal Notice 6.4 and 6.7: the script reads fictional lab files only; keep everything fictional.
Versions and look (October 2026): Python 3.15.1 (October 21, 2026) is the current release; any Python 3.8 or later runs the script, with no module to install. On Windows, the Python install manager (py install 3.15) replaces the classic installer, which disappears with Python 3.16; the prompt and colours of your terminal will differ from the drawing.
4

Run code example 2 — the network map

Part E — 25 points (data)
Animated screens drawn for this guide; the terminal outputs are the real outputs of the scripts. Click the picture to enlarge.
  • cd code/example2_network_map then python kalmia_netmap.py net_devices.csv subnets.csv flows.csv
  • [PLACE] and [CHECK] verify tags, addresses and links; [ZONE] and [FLOW] rate the zones and the 16 flows (TRUST-BOUNDARY, UNKNOWN, DECISION-NEEDED).
  • Three files appear: physical_view.mmd and logical_view.mmd (Mermaid text for draw.io, step 5) and network_map_check.csv → sheet Map findings. Paste net_devices.csv, subnets.csv and flows.csv into Network devices, Subnets and Flows.
Rule: Legal Notice 6.1 and 7.1: no scan, no live system — the map is built from the lab files; the Class 2 authorization covered one range, one window, one exercise.
Versions and look (October 2026): Same Python as step 3. The real output has 77 lines; the drawing shows the beginning and the end (the full text is in expected_output/console_output.txt).
5

Draw the two views in draw.io

Part E — 25 points (diagrams)
Animated screens drawn for this guide; the terminal outputs are the real outputs of the scripts. Click the picture to enlarge.
  • Open app.diagrams.net (no install) or draw.io desktop. Menu Arrange › Insert › Mermaid…, paste the whole text of physical_view.mmd, keep Diagram (the text becomes shapes you can move), click Insert.
  • Complete the drawing: a title block (title, version 1.0, date, author, data source), a legend, the word Confidential, and the same hostnames and asset tags as the Hardware sheet. Resolve the two untagged devices (LOG-ROAST-01, EXT-WH-01): register them or record their removal.
  • File › Save as › physical_view.drawio and File › Export as › PDF (or PNG, Portable Network Graphics) › physical_view.pdf, both in diagrams/. Repeat with logical_view.mmd: zones, the trust boundary and the 16 flows must be visible. Tick the Diagram checklist sheet.
Rule: Legal Notice 7.5: a network diagram shows an attacker where the valuable systems are — label it Confidential, keep it in your course folder, share it only with the professor.
Versions and look (October 2026): draw.io 32.5.5 (web and desktop, October 18, 2026). The documentation also shows the path Arrange › Insert › Advanced › Mermaid in some versions; the dialog and the export menu may look different after an update — the menu names stay the same. Free alternatives: yEd, Excalidraw, LibreOffice Draw, Mermaid Live Editor.
6

Fill the workbook and export six sheets as CSV UTF-8

Parts B, C, D, E, F — the workbook
Animated screens drawn for this guide; the terminal outputs are the real outputs of the scripts. Click the picture to enlarge.
  • Open each output CSV (comma-separated values) file in Excel or LibreOffice Calc, copy its rows, and paste them as values (Paste Special › Values) under the headers of the matching sheet. Teal headers are filled by tools, amber headers by you: owner, decision, approval.
  • Part C comes from Class 2: hw_reconciled.csv → Hardware (every device with an owner), software_inventory.csv → Software, permission_findings.csv → Admin rights.
  • Export six sheets: select the sheet, File › Save As › CSV UTF-8 (Comma delimited) — UTF-8 (Unicode Transformation Format, 8-bit) keeps accented letters — (LibreOffice: Text CSV, character set Unicode (UTF-8)) into workbook/csv/: hardware.csv, software.csv, critical_services.csv, network_devices.csv, permissions_map.csv, access_review.csv.
Rule: Legal Notice 6.7 and 18.2: fictional data only in every cell — never a real name, address, account or document.
Versions and look (October 2026): Excel (Microsoft 365, October 2026) and LibreOffice 26.8 (August 2026) place the file type in the Save As dialog; Google Sheets exports with File › Download › Comma-separated values. Excel exports only the active sheet — repeat for the six sheets.
7

Run code example 3 — the permissions map (PowerShell)

Part F — 15 points
Animated screens drawn for this guide; the terminal outputs are the real outputs of the scripts. Click the picture to enlarge.
  • Windows: open PowerShell, cd code\example3_permissions_map, then Unblock-File .\Get-KalmiaPermissionsMap.ps1, Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned (answer Y) and .\Get-KalmiaPermissionsMap.ps1 -InputFolder .\perms
  • The script expands the groups, computes the effective access of 14 accounts on 6 shares and prints the findings: EXCESS, MISSING, ORPHAN, SHARED, DIRECT-ACE, NO-MFA (multi-factor authentication), SOD (separation of duties) — 20 findings, 10 HIGH.
  • Paste role_matrix.csv → Role matrix, permissions_map.csv → Permissions map, access_findings.csv → Access review, then write the Owner and a Decision (keep, reduce, remove, accept) for every finding — every HIGH finding decided. No Windows? Use the files of expected_output/.
Rule: Legal Notice 6.1 and 6.7: the real mode of the script (Get-Acl on a real folder) runs only on a folder you own or are authorized to review — never on the shares of an employer or a school.
Versions and look (October 2026): Windows PowerShell 5.1 (built into Windows 10 and 11, blue window) and PowerShell 7.6.8 (October 22, 2026, black window) both run the script; the drawing shows the 5.1 colours. The execution policy prompt appears only the first time. Alternatives for real permissions: icacls (built in) and AccessEnum (Sysinternals).
8

Write the one-page memo and save it as PDF

Part G — 10 points
Animated screens drawn for this guide; the terminal outputs are the real outputs of the scripts. Click the picture to enlarge.
  • One page for Nadia Roy, president of Kalmia: who it is for, from whom, the date, the word Confidential — then the five findings she must know first, in business terms (what can stop, what can leak, for how long), and the decision you ask for each.
  • Numbers come from your workbook (an MTD, a restore time, a count of accounts). No real person, no real company, no number in the format of a SIN (Social Insurance Number) or of a payment card — the checker treats them as a BLOCKER.
  • Save it as PDF (Portable Document Format) in memo/: Word or Writer › Save As / Export › PDF; macOS Pages › Export To › PDF.
Rule: Legal Notice 6.7 and 18.2: no real personal information in a lab file, ever; 7.5: the memo lists weaknesses — Confidential.
Versions and look (October 2026): Word (Microsoft 365), LibreOffice Writer 26.8, Google Docs (File › Download › PDF) and Pages all export a PDF; the dialog drawn here is generic.
9

Run the readiness checker, fix, reach 100%

Before the hand-in — code example 4
Animated screens drawn for this guide; the terminal outputs are the real outputs of the scripts. Click the picture to enlarge.
  • From the folder that contains your Lab 1 folder (Git Bash on Windows, Terminal on macOS and Linux): bash lab1_check.sh Lab1_Lastname_Firstname
  • One line per check: [OK] passed, [TODO] something to add or fix, [BLOCKER] a number that looks like a SIN or a card — the folder must not be submitted as it is. The sample folder of code example 4 starts at 70% with seven TODO lines and one BLOCKER: practise on it.
  • Fix in order: the blocker, then the content (RTO < MTD, owners, decisions, untagged devices), then the presentation (exports, memo, README). Export the sheets again and run the checker again until blocker=0 todo=0 readiness=100%. The report lab1_readiness.txt is written next to your folder, not inside it.
Rule: The checker is the privacy control of section 18.2 made visible: a SIN-like or card-like number blocks the submission.
Versions and look (October 2026): The outputs shown are the real outputs of lab1_check.sh on the sample folder before and after the fixes. The script needs Bash with awk, grep and paste (Git Bash 2.56, macOS Terminal, any Linux). The checker proves that nothing is missing; the professor judges the quality.
10

Compress the folder and submit it in Léa

The hand-in — Thursday, November 5, 2026, midnight (23:59), Eastern Time
Animated screens drawn for this guide; the terminal outputs are the real outputs of the scripts. Click the picture to enlarge.
  • Right-click the folder › Compress to… › ZIP file (macOS: Compress) → Lab1_Lastname_Firstname.zip. The ZIP contains the folder itself; the report stays outside.
  • Omnivox › Léa › 420-1C2-DW › Assignments › Lab 1 — Asset inventory and infrastructure map › Submit › choose the ZIP › send. Keep the confirmation. You may resubmit until the deadline; the last file counts.
  • Only the Léa drop box is accepted — no e-mail, no MIO (Omnivox's internal messaging). Late work loses 10% per day; nothing is accepted seven days after the due date (course outline).
Rule: Legal Notice 17.2 and 18.1: the work is your own; the lab files, credentials and course links stay in the cohort. Daylight saving time ends on November 1, 2026: the Léa clock is the reference.
Versions and look (October 2026): The Léa screens are drawn for this guide: the real labels (Assignments, Travaux, Submit, Déposer) and the page layout depend on the version of Omnivox used by your college in November 2026. Windows 11 compresses with Compress to… › ZIP file; Windows 10 says Send to › Compressed (zipped) folder; 7-Zip 26.05 is a free alternative.

The rules of this lab — Cyber.SoHo Legal Notice v2.0

Authorization (6.1, 7.1) — Lab 1 touches no live system; the scripts read the lab files only. The Class 2 authorization covered one range, one window, one exercise. “If you are not certain that you have authorization, you do not have it.”
Lab environment (6.4) — In a virtual machine: isolate it, take a snapshot first, clean up afterwards; keep everything fictional.
Software and downloads (6.6, 14, Annex C) — Official sources only, checksums verified, no cracked software; keep your system, browser and security software up to date.
Data and privacy (6.7, 18.2) — Fictional or synthetic data only — never the accounts, permissions, logs or documents of a real person or organization; no screenshots with real credentials or internal addresses.
Accidental discovery (6.8) · this course (7.3) — If a real weakness ever appears in front of you: stop, copy nothing, tell only the owner, report it. Study threat information; never visit live malicious infrastructure, contact threat actors or download breach data.
Confidential findings (7.5) — Your workbook, diagrams and memo show what an attacker looks for: course folder only, shared only with the professor; course work is never an audit.
Real organizations (7.9) — Never your employer's, a client's or a relative's systems or data; Annex D is the only form of permission, and your employer's rules take precedence.
Recording, confidentiality, your work (17, 18, 4.1–4.3) — No recording or screen capture of classes without written permission; lab files, credentials and course links stay in the cohort; the submission is your own and you keep its copyright; the course materials are licensed, not sold — do not redistribute them. The student acknowledgement (Annex A, e-signature) is provided separately.
